title: A morphism of modules on a scheme is an isomorphism iff it is bijective on all stalks
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ a morphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules (sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules on the Zariski topology of $X$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]). For $x\in X$ let $\mathcal F_x=\varinjlim_{U\ni x}\mathcal F(U)$ be the stalk (colimit over the open neighbourhoods of $x$) and $\varphi_x:\mathcal F_x\to\mathcal G_x$ the induced map. Then $\varphi$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules if and only if $\varphi_x$ is bijective for every $x\in X$.

source.place: Sheaves, Tag 007T (label lemma-points-exactness, part (3): a map of sheaves of sets is an isomorphism iff it is bijective on all stalks), applied to the underlying sheaves of sets, with Modules, Tag 01AG (label lemma-abelian: Mod(O_X) is abelian, kernels and cokernels computed stalkwise); the inverse of an O_X-linear bijective map of sheaves is O_X-linear
